page: Amazon Web Services c6a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at up to 3.6 GHz, it features 48 physical CPU cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs with 2.0 threads per core. The instance includes 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware instruction extensions include AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, FMA, and baseline AVX, though AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. It carries no local block storage and features a 38 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluation demonstrates top-tier multi-core computational capability, evidenced by stress-ng multi-core performance in the top 10% of tested instances (143,412.53) and high Geekbench ray tracing performance (90,953.0). Encryption workloads benefit from hardware acceleration, yielding top-tier PassMark CPU encryption scores (109,006.43). In memory-bound scenarios, the system shows strong cached L1/L2 read throughput (6,133.95 GB/sec), whereas uncached DDR4 memory read and write bandwidth remain in the middle 50% percentile (132.64 GB/sec and 60.64 GB/sec, respectively). In-memory database processing remains efficient, with Redis SET operations achieving 89.64 million operations per second.

From an architecture and cost perspective, c6a.24xlarge delivers high vCPU density without paying for integrated local NVMe storage, making it cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads reliant on attached network storage or stateless scaling. The main resource constraint is the 2.0 GB per vCPU memory capacity, which limits memory-dense applications. Suitable workloads include software compilation, video and image rendering, high-throughput web service backend compute, batch processing, cryptography operations, and small-to-medium scale LLM inference prompt processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c6a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by an AMD EPYC 7R13 x86_64 processor with 48 physical cores, 96 dedicated vCPUs at 3.6 GHz, and 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with 38 Gbps network bandwidth and no local storage, it offers a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio optimized for raw CPU performance. Synthetic testing shows top-tier multi-core CPU capacity, highlighted by high stress-ng multi-core metrics, accelerated AES/VAES hardware encryption, and strong software compilation throughput. While uncached DDR4 memory bandwidth ranks in the average range, high-density vCPU allocation yields efficient compute scaling for workloads requiring heavy parallel execution without local disk overhead. It is well-suited for parallelized software builds, batch cryptography, distributed compute nodes, and high-volume Redis operations.
